This application coming on for hearing this day, the Co  following:
 ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicants/accused,
relating to FIR/Crime No.73/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Tanda,
District Dhar (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376,

sentences.text: 2 . Prosecution story in brief is that on 24.03.2023, at around 8.00 PM, when the prosecutrix was at grocery shop, co-accused Dharmendra and Dinesh came there on motorcycle where co-accused Dinesh forcefully made her sit on the motorcycle and both of them took the prosecutrix to Village Bavdi, thereafter co-accused Dharmendra left and co-accused Dinesh kept her there for 05 days and committed rape upon the prosecutrix.
On 01.04.2023, prosecutrix lodged an FIR against the co-accused persons Dharmendra and Dinesh.

Co-accused Dinesh is brother-in-law of the prosecutrix and co- accused Dharmendra is brother-in-law of co-accused Dinesh and the present applicants have been implicated on the basis of memorandum statement of co- accused persons recorded under Section 27 of the Indian Evidence Act.
At the time of incident, prosecutrix was aged about 17 years 10 months.

3 . Learned counsel for the applicants submits that name of the present applicants/accused have not been mentioned in the FIR, case diary statement of prosecutrix as well as statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. Co- accused Dharmendra has been granted bail by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 01.06.2023 in MCRC No.22703/2023.

After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed and the trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that present applicants/accused be released on bail.
4 . On the other hand, learned Government Advocate for the non- applicant/State has objected the prayer and prayed for rejection of the application.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the fact trial will take sufficient long time for its conclusion, this Court is of the view that applicants deserve to be enlarged on bail, hence, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that applicants- Santosh & Anarbai shall be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) each alongwith one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court, for their appearance before the concerned Court regularly on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during trial.

It is further directed that applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C.
7.
With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE gp Santosh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182442066/
